To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) layer 5 pyramids in mouse vibrissa cortex produce a distributed and nonlinear network representation that is used to generate motor commands during adaptive sensing; (2) this representation is generated via active dendritic computation; and (3) the representation is required for mice adaptively to adjust their sensorimotor behavior.

layer 5 of the vibrissae barrel cortex generates a diverse and distributed network population representation of joint sensor–motor parameters that is required to transform sensory information to motor commands during active sensing behavior.

(1) active dendritic integration produces a nonlinearly distributed representation of joint sensor–motor parameters; (2) this representation is used to transform the sensory information into motor command during active sensing; (3) this representation is required for adaptive whisking behavior; and (4) this representation is degraded by selective inhibition of dendritic integration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of active sensory–motor transformations during behavior.
the neuronal mechanisms underlying the sensory-motor transformation in the neocortex, and the role of the neocortex in active sensing behavior.
the neural mechanisms of active sensing.

active dendritic computation is necessary for the formation of a mixed population encoding in layer 5 pyramids that is used to generate adaptive whisking behavior in mice.
the authors show that active dendritic integrations in layer 5 of the vibrissae barrel cortex are required for mice to perform an active sensing task.

active dendritic computation in layer 5 pyramids produces a nonlinearly encoded, mixed network population representation of sensorimotor parameters used to adapt motor strategy to changing environmental conditions during active sensing.

layer 5 of vibrissa cortex uses active dendritic integration and a diverse and distributed network of neurons to represent the joint parameters of sensorimotor transformations during an adaptive sensing task.
active dendritic integrative mechanisms generate a nonlinear, mixed network representation of sensory–motor variables that is used to drive adaptive behavior.

the layer 5 circuit motif is a general cortical computation that is required for adaptive behavior.
